name: Sphingolipid degradation
summary: Lysosomes take glycosphingolipids apart one group at a time, down to ceramide. Each missing enzyme is a lysosomal storage disease, all autosomal recessive except Fabry (X-linked recessive). Cherry-red macula: Tay-Sachs and Niemann-Pick. Hepatosplenomegaly: Gaucher and Niemann-Pick, not Tay-Sachs. Demyelination: Krabbe and metachromatic leukodystrophy.

ceramide.name: Ceramide
ceramide.notes: Sphingosine + fatty acid: the core of every sphingolipid. Ceramidase then splits it (deficient in Farber disease).

bgal.name: β-Galactosidase (GM1)
bgal.notes: Deficiency → GM1 gangliosidosis: neurodegeneration, hepatosplenomegaly, coarse facies, cherry-red spot.

hexa.name: Hexosaminidase A
hexa.notes: Deficiency → Tay-Sachs: progressive neurodegeneration, developmental delay, hyperreflexia, hyperacusis (exaggerated startle), cherry-red macula, lysosomes with onion-skin inclusions; NO hepatosplenomegaly. ↑ in Ashkenazi Jews.

hexab.name: Hexosaminidase A and B
hexab.notes: Deficiency of the shared β subunit → Sandhoff: like Tay-Sachs plus hepatosplenomegaly (GM2 and globoside both build up).

agal.name: α-Galactosidase A
agal.notes: Deficiency → Fabry (X-linked recessive): early peripheral neuropathy of hands and feet (pain), angiokeratomas, hypohidrosis; later renal failure and cardiovascular disease. Treat with enzyme replacement.

gba.name: β-Glucocerebrosidase
gba.notes: Deficiency → Gaucher (most common): hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, osteoporosis, avascular necrosis of the femur, bone crises; Gaucher cells (lipid-laden macrophages like crumpled tissue paper). Treat with recombinant enzyme (imiglucerase).

asa.name: Arylsulfatase A
asa.notes: Deficiency → metachromatic leukodystrophy: central and peripheral demyelination with ataxia, dementia.

galc.name: Galactocerebrosidase
galc.notes: Deficiency → Krabbe: peripheral neuropathy, destruction of oligodendrocytes (psychosine), developmental delay, optic atrophy, globoid cells.

smase.name: Sphingomyelinase
smase.notes: Deficiency → Niemann-Pick: progressive neurodegeneration, hepatosplenomegaly, foam cells (lipid-laden macrophages), cherry-red macula. ↑ in Ashkenazi Jews. 'No man picks (Niemann-Pick) his nose with his sphinger (sphingomyelinase).'

diseases.name: Tay–Sachs disease
diseases.clue: Progressive neurodegeneration with an exaggerated startle and a cherry-red macula, but no hepatosplenomegaly; onion-skin lysosomes.

diseases.name: Gaucher disease
diseases.clue: Hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia and bone pain or avascular necrosis; “crumpled tissue paper” macrophages. Most common lysosomal storage disease.

diseases.name: Sandhoff disease
diseases.clue: Like Tay–Sachs (cherry-red macula, neurodegeneration) but with hepatosplenomegaly.

diseases.name: Fabry disease
diseases.clue: Burning pain in hands and feet, angiokeratomas, hypohidrosis, then kidney and heart failure; X-linked.

diseases.name: Metachromatic leukodystrophy
diseases.clue: Central and peripheral demyelination: ataxia and dementia.

diseases.name: Krabbe disease
diseases.clue: Peripheral neuropathy, developmental delay and optic atrophy with globoid cells.

diseases.name: Niemann–Pick disease
diseases.clue: Progressive neurodegeneration, hepatosplenomegaly, cherry-red macula and foam cells.

tissue: every cell's lysosomes (brain, liver, spleen, bone matter most)
